findings.title: Direct-capture acquisition mode (the provenance channel label) is chosen by the client in the open-session body; any signed-in API client can mint 'PROOVRA iOS/Android app' or 'PROOVRA extension' Evidence
findings.userImpact: A reviewer sees 'iOS screen recording - PROOVRA app (client-attested)' / 'Web capture - PROOVRA extension' on records that may have been produced by a script using an ordinary web session token.
findings.legalImpact: Channel provenance (which PROOVRA client produced the bytes) is not established by the server even though code comments claim it is; the only mitigation is the 'client-attested' wording of the descriptors.
findings.securityImpact: No privilege escalation; provenance forgery by any authenticated user within their own workspace.
findings.reproduction: With a normal web AUTH_JWT: POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions {mode:'DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS'} -> POST .../:id/evidence -> POST /v1/evidence/:eid/parts (not extension-scoped, so extensionMayPresignPart is not consulted) + PUT arbitrary bytes -> POST .../parts/:n/declaration with their sha256 -> build a continuity manifest with platform 'ios' listing those parts, upload+declare it -> POST .../:id/continuous-complete. Evidence.acquisitionMode = DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS, RECORDED_AT_CREATION.
findings.observed: OpenDirectSessionBody.mode = z.enum(DIRECT_CAPTURE_SESSION_MODES) is copied verbatim into CaptureSession.acquisitionMode (direct-capture-ingest.service.ts:294) and then into Evidence.acquisitionMode by reserve; no binding to token type, client id, device key or platform attestation. deviceId is optional and never sent by any client.
findings.expected: Mode derived from an authenticated client identity (extension-scoped token => DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION only; mobile client credential/attestation => mobile modes), or the descriptor must not name the client as the producer.
findings.rootCause: UC-0 treats 'server-issued session' as the authority for mode, but the server issues whatever mode the caller requests.
findings.remediation: Bind allowed modes to the credential: restrict extension-scoped tokens to DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION at open; require a registered device + attestation (or an app-client credential) for mobile/screen modes, or downgrade unauthenticated-client sessions to a generic mode; correct the comments at continuous-capture.service.ts:25/70 and evidence.service.ts:251.
findings.requiredTests: Route test: web JWT opening DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS / DIRECT_WEB_CAPTURE_EXTENSION is refused or recorded as a non-app mode; extension token opening PROOVRA_MOBILE_APP refused.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB + API: execute the reproduction with a password-login JWT; assert evidence.acquisition_mode = 'DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS' and the report acquisition section names the iOS app.

findings.title: Workspace default retention (and capture-environment/template stamping) is applied only by the web POST /v1/evidence route and intake orchestration; mobile, extension, Android and iOS captures never receive retentionUntilUtc
findings.userImpact: In a Team workspace with a retention policy, records captured by the mobile app or extension carry no retention date and are eligible for trash/delete immediately, unlike identical web uploads.
findings.legalImpact: Retention-policy compliance differs by capture channel; records the workspace policy says must be kept can be deleted.
findings.reproduction: Set defaultRetentionDays on a Team workspace policy; capture via POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions (mode PROOVRA_MOBILE_APP, teamId=team) -> reserve -> part -> declaration -> complete. evidence.retention_until_utc stays NULL; the same file via web POST /v1/evidence gets now+N days.
findings.observed: applyRetentionPolicyOnCreate is called at evidence.routes.ts:5631 and external-intake-orchestration.service.ts:452 only; resolveRetentionOnCreate/applyRetentionPolicyOnCreate have no other caller, and neither createEvidence nor completeEvidence applies it. recordCaptureEnvironment likewise only at evidence.routes.ts:5594 and external-intake.routes.ts:1126/1319.
findings.expected: Retention-on-create applied inside createEvidence (the canonical writer) for every channel.
findings.rootCause: Lifecycle side effects implemented in route handlers instead of the canonical createEvidence service.
findings.remediation: Move applyRetentionPolicyOnCreate into createEvidence (inside writeRecord or afterCommit) and delete the per-route calls; add a reconciler for existing direct-capture rows in retention-policy workspaces.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: same workspace policy, one record per acquisition mode; all have retention_until_utc = created + N days.
findings.migrationImpact: additive (backfill of retention_until_utc for direct-capture rows)
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable PG: policy defaultRetentionDays=30, create one web and one direct-capture record, compare retention_until_utc.

findings.title: Completion fan-out (EVIDENCE_COMPLETED custody event, reviewer-workflow initialization, evidence.create/complete tenant audit) exists only in the web route handlers; direct-capture and intake records never enter the reviewer queue and lack the completion custody event
findings.userImpact: Intake submissions and mobile/extension/screen captures do not appear in reviewer queues (queues read EvidenceReviewWorkflow rows) until someone manually opens the reviewer workflow; custody timelines and reports differ by channel.
findings.legalImpact: Custody chain content depends on channel: web records carry EVIDENCE_COMPLETED, others do not. The intake orchestration comment claims it does.
findings.securityImpact: Tenant audit log has no evidence.create/evidence.complete rows for direct-capture records (only part presign audits via /v1/evidence/:id/parts).
findings.reproduction: Complete one record via POST /v1/capture/direct-sessions/:id/complete and one via public intake submit; SELECT from custody_events WHERE event_type='EVIDENCE_COMPLETED' and from evidence_review_workflows for both -> no rows; the web-upload record has both.
findings.observed: EVIDENCE_COMPLETED appended only at evidence.routes.ts:10507; upsertEvidenceReviewerWorkflow called only at evidence.routes.ts:8474 (manual PATCH) and :10561; EvidenceReviewWorkflow otherwise created only by ensureReviewWorkflow (ops seed / reviewer engine).
findings.expected: completeEvidence (or its fan-out) performs every channel-independent post-finalize step once.
findings.rootCause: Same as UC-ARCH-002 on the completion side: route-resident fan-out.
findings.remediation: Move EVIDENCE_COMPLETED custody (in the completion transaction), reviewer workflow upsert and tenant audit into completeEvidence/runCompletionFanoutOnce; fix the stale comment at external-intake-orchestration.service.ts:996-1000.
findings.requiredTests: Cross-channel conservation test: for each acquisition mode, completion yields identical custody event types and one EvidenceReviewWorkflow row.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB: finalize via each of the three finalizer callers and diff custody event types + review workflow rows.

findings.title: API-key resumable upload channel (/v1/integrations/api/uploads/*) can never open a session: it passes the API credential id as the OWNER principal, which never equals Evidence.ownerUserId
findings.userImpact: Enterprise integrations with integration.evidence.upload scope always receive 404 evidence_not_found; the documented machine-ingest channel is unusable.
findings.reproduction: Create an API key with integration.evidence.upload for team T; POST /v1/integrations/api/uploads/sessions {evidenceId: <any T evidence in UPLOADING>, idempotencyKey, expectedPartCount:1} -> createUploadSession -> assertEvidenceAcceptsByteWrites(OWNER, userId=credentialId) -> lockEvidenceForByteWrite throws EVIDENCE_NOT_FOUND -> 404.
findings.observed: actorUserId: cred.credentialId (routes :338/:485/:618); ET-UPL-01 added the owner byte-write check at upload-session.service.ts:393-396 without an API-credential principal. No API route can create Evidence either, so there is no record an integration could own. Tests are source-regex only.
findings.expected: Either a SERVICE_ACCOUNT principal with its own authority, or the routes retired (410) and removed from docs.
findings.rootCause: Byte-write authority has only OWNER and INTAKE_SESSION principals; the integration path was not migrated when ET-UPL-01 was remediated.
findings.remediation: Decide: add an explicit INTEGRATION principal (team-bound, record created for the integration) or retire the 9 routes with 410; fix the header comment (routes 511-606 exist though the header says multipart is out of scope).
findings.requiredTests: Behavioural integration test with a real API key creating and completing a session.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB + API: seed API key + evidence, call the create route, assert 404 evidence_not_found.

findings.title: The intake link creator can inject parts into, or prematurely finalize, a contributor's in-flight intake record through the authenticated /v1/evidence/:id/parts and /complete routes
findings.userImpact: A sealed 'Submitted through a secure intake link' record can contain files the contributor never sent, or be sealed before the contributor finished (their later submit then fails).
findings.legalImpact: Third-party submission integrity: intake records are presented as contributor-sourced but the workspace-side owner can alter their content before sealing.
findings.securityImpact: Insider-only (the Evidence owner = link creator); bypasses intake session state, part caps and reserveIntakeLinkUse.
findings.reproduction: Link creator opens GET /v1/workflow/intake-links/:id/submissions (evidenceId of in-progress sessions is projected, intake-link-lifecycle.service.ts:739); while the contributor is uploading (status UPLOADING), POST /v1/evidence/:eid/parts {partIndex: 50} + PUT bytes, then POST /v1/evidence/:eid/complete.
findings.observed: Intake Evidence is owned by link.createdByUserId; lockEvidenceForByteWrite admits OWNER=that user; completeEvidence guards only UC-0 capture sessions (acquisitionMode not null) and has no SECURE_INTAKE_LINK check.
findings.expected: A record whose acquisitionMode is SECURE_INTAKE_LINK accepts parts and completion only through the intake session (INTAKE_SESSION principal / submitExternalIntake).
findings.rootCause: Intake records reuse the owner's byte-write and completion authority instead of a session-bound one like UC-0.
findings.remediation: In lockEvidenceForByteWrite and completeEvidence refuse OWNER principals on records bound to a non-terminal WorkflowIntakeSession (or on acquisitionMode SECURE_INTAKE_LINK) unless called by the intake orchestration.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: owner POST /parts and /complete on an intake-bound UPLOADING record -> 409.
findings.runtimeProbe: Disposable DB: create link, open contributor session, upload one part, then as link creator add a part and complete; assert the sealed record lists both parts and acquisition SECURE_INTAKE_LINK.

findings.title: Multipart composite digest and streaming SHA-256 are implemented three times (API completion, worker integrity recheck, worker report gate) with no shared authority
findings.legalImpact: Drift risk: a change to one copy would make the integrity recheck or report gate declare correctly sealed evidence FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH.
findings.reproduction: Read the three sites: sha256(partHashes.join('|')) each, ordered by partIndex asc via independent queries (evidence-complete.service.ts:804, integrity-recheck.ts:303).
findings.observed: Three private copies of the composite rule plus a legacy single-part-composite special case only in the worker.
findings.expected: One exported digest builder in packages/shared(-runtime) used by all three.
findings.remediation: Extract compositeSha256/sha256HexFromStream to shared-runtime and import everywhere.
findings.requiredTests: Golden-vector test shared by API and worker.

findings.title: Device-bound signing, device registration, platform attestation and trust-timeline surfaces have no client caller; every production direct-capture session is unbound and unsigned
findings.userImpact: Security Center lists capture devices that no client can register; 'deviceBound' and signed declarations never occur.
findings.legalImpact: Code-complete claims for device-signed capture are not reachable in product.
findings.reproduction: grep apps/{web,mobile,extension} for POST /v1/capture/devices, /attestation, /trust-timeline: none (web only lists/revokes devices, CaptureDevicesSection.tsx:118,172). Mobile sends { mode[, teamId] } and signed:null; extension sends deviceId:null.
findings.expected: Either wire the mobile client (key generation + registration + attestation) or mark the surfaces unshipped.
findings.rootCause: Server-first build without the native client half.
findings.remediation: Implement or explicitly de-scope; keep UC-ARCH-001 in mind (device binding is the natural mode authority).

findings.title: createEvidence always mints a root presigned PUT URL and records UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED for the 'initial location', but no client ever uploads to it (all channels upload parts)
findings.legalImpact: Custody event UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED states a URL was issued for evidence/{id}/original-* on web/mobile/extension records whose bytes never go there; for intake it says 'No upload URL was issued' while one is minted (not delivered) at evidence.service.ts:674.
findings.securityImpact: A live 10-minute write URL to the root key is returned to web callers of POST /v1/evidence and ignored.
findings.reproduction: grep apps for upload.putUrl: only part-presign responses are used (useCaptureSessionOrchestration.ts:863, intake page.tsx:795, mobile direct-capture.ts:165, extension background.ts:76/123).
findings.expected: No root presign; custody event describes the actual part-based upload.
findings.rootCause: Pre-multipart single-object design retained in the canonical writer.
findings.remediation: Stop presigning in createEvidence (or only on explicit request); reword UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED.
findings.requiredTests: createEvidence returns no putUrl; custody payload wording test.

findings.title: The browser extension never discards its direct-capture session on failure; the reserved Evidence lingers until the capture-reaper expiry
findings.userImpact: A failed web capture leaves a reserved empty record for up to the session TTL (1h sliding) before the worker releases it.
findings.reproduction: runPreserve has no try/catch around steps 55-130 and api-client.ts has no discard call (mobile uses sealDirectCapture -> /discard, apps/mobile/src/direct-capture.ts:266-292).
findings.observed: Recovery relies solely on the reaper.
findings.rootCause: Mobile fix (sealDirectCapture) not ported to the extension.
findings.remediation: Add discardSession to api-client and wrap runPreserve; add /discard to the scope allowlist (already covered by the direct-sessions prefix).
findings.requiredTests: Extension unit test: failing upload triggers /discard.
